documents.unit: AI Steering Council / AI Task Force
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Acceptable Use Policy
documents.summary: University-wide acceptable use policy from the provost's office covering teaching, research and administration. It sets data, legal and ethics duties and tells instructors to write their own syllabus AI policy.
documents.stance_why: It sets no AI stance for coursework itself; it says there 'will be disciplinary differences' and that 'Instructors should include a policy in all their syllabi', and sends academic integrity to existing rules.

units.why: The purpose clause sets the policy's aim: 'ethical, transparent, and responsible use of Artificial Intelligence'. It is an institution-wide framework statement, so P56, general, informs.
units.anchor: ethical, transparent, and responsible use of Artificial Intelligence

units.why: 'This policy will be revisited and updated as AI evolves' commits to revision, so P54 (revisit regularly), over-time, informs.
units.anchor: This policy will be revisited and updated as AI evolves.

units.why: The scope clause says the policy 'applies to all members of the Brandeis community'. It sets what the policy covers, so P61 (scope) rather than P56 which is the purpose and principles.
units.anchor: applies to all members of the Brandeis community, including students, faculty, staff, and affiliates

units.why: Defines AI as 'Computer systems designed to do tasks that usually require human intelligence'; a definition setting coverage, P61.
units.anchor: Computer systems designed to do tasks that usually require human intelligence.

units.why: Defines generative AI as a subset 'designed to create new content, such as text, images, music, or code'; a definition, P61.
units.anchor: designed to create new content, such as text, images, music, or code

units.why: Defines machine learning AI as learning 'without the generation of new content'; a definition that sets what the policy covers, P61.
units.anchor: focuses on learning from existing data without the generation of new content

units.why: 'All AI applications must comply with Brandeis' data governance protocols and cybersecurity policies' binds all users on data handling; P50 (protect data), must, restrict.
units.anchor: All AI applications must comply with Brandeis' data governance protocols and cybersecurity policies.

units.why: 'Use of regulated, restricted, or confidential information in AI tools requires appropriate authorization and safeguards' limits data entered into AI, P50, must, restrict.
units.anchor: Use of regulated, restricted, or confidential information in AI tools requires appropriate authorization and safeguards.

units.why: Everyone 'must ensure that AI tools are used ethically, maintaining the integrity and originality of their work', which makes users responsible for the originality of their own work (P29) rather than naming a concrete ethics concern (P53).
units.anchor: must ensure that AI tools are used ethically, maintaining the integrity and originality
units.frag_end: integrity and originality of their work.

units.why: 'must adhere to applicable laws and legal obligations when using AI' with IP and FERPA named; legal and IP compliance fits P52 better than P50 because the passage is about legal rights.
units.anchor: must adhere to applicable laws and legal obligations when using AI
units.frag_end: and other privacy laws, and other regulations.

units.why: Members 'must comply with applicable contracts, end user agreements, and other terms' of AI tools; terms of use, P52.
units.anchor: must comply with applicable contracts, end user agreements, and other terms

units.why: 'Instructors should include a policy in all their syllabi regarding the use (and misuse) of generative AI' is a syllabus-statement requirement, P09, before-course, should.
units.anchor: include a policy in all their syllabi regarding the use (and misuse) of generative AI

units.why: Instructors should 'dedicate some time in class discussing the reasons for how AI can be used', which communicates expectations; P09 fits as the nearest communication type.
units.anchor: dedicate some time in class discussing the reasons for how AI can be used

units.why: 'there will be disciplinary differences in how AI is integrated into coursework depending on learning objectives' leaves the AI rule to instructors and disciplines, P04, informs.
units.anchor: there will be disciplinary differences in how AI is integrated into coursework
units.frag_start: Under this policy, there will be

units.why: Students 'are expected to maintain the University's standards of academic integrity, including the use of artificial intelligence'. This ties AI use to existing integrity rules, so P36 fits better than P29 (the passage invokes integrity standards, not ownership of submitted work).
units.anchor: expected to maintain the University's standards of academic integrity, including the use of artificial intelligence

units.why: 'AI-generated content should be critically evaluated and not solely relied upon for research conclusions' tells researchers to verify AI output; P31 chosen over P62 because the content is verification.
units.anchor: AI-generated content should be critically evaluated and not solely relied upon for research conclusions

units.why: 'Regulated, restricted, and confidential data should never be input into AI tools without proper safeguards' is a data rule in the research section, P50, should-not.
units.anchor: should never be input into AI tools without proper safeguards and approvals

units.why: 'the author, not the technology, is accountable' holds researchers responsible for AI-assisted work, P29.
units.anchor: the author, not the technology, is accountable

units.why: Researchers using AI in human subjects research 'must consult with the Brandeis Human Research Protection Program', a research rule, P62, must.
units.anchor: must consult with the Brandeis Human Research Protection Program (HRPP)

units.why: 'use of AI in preparing publications and grant proposals may be restricted by publisher and funder policies' defers to venue and funder rules, P62.
units.anchor: may be restricted by publisher and funder policies
units.frag_start: The use of AI in preparing
units.frag_end: Limiting Submissions per PI | Grants & Funding

units.why: 'Staff are also encouraged to explore AI tools to enhance efficiency in administrative tasks' welcomes staff AI use by default, P02 (no type covers staff administrative use better), encourage.
units.anchor: Staff are also encouraged to explore AI tools to enhance efficiency in administrative tasks
units.frag_start: Staff are also encouraged to explore

units.why: 'Employees are required to use University-approved and provided AI tools if using University data' pushes vetted tools, P50.
units.anchor: Employees are required to use University-approved and provided AI tools if using University data

units.why: 'Departments seeking to acquire AI tools must follow the university's procurement policies and obtain necessary approvals' sets review of AI acquisitions, P65.
units.anchor: must follow the university's procurement policies and obtain necessary approvals

units.why: 'Violations of this policy will be addressed in accordance with existing university procedures for academic and administrative misconduct' classifies violations as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: Violations of this policy will be addressed in accordance with existing university procedures

units.why: 'The AI Task Force will periodically review and update this policy' names who maintains and reviews the policy, P54.
units.anchor: The AI Task Force will periodically review and update this policy

units.why: Directs people to the CTL 'for guidance on AI use in teaching and learning', a support resource for instructors, P63.
units.anchor: contact the Center for Teaching and Learning (CTL) at ctl@brandeis.edu

documents.title: AI Syllabus Statements
tiers: Policy B1 (situational; permitted for background learning)
Policy B2 (situational; permitted for refining assignments)
documents.summary: CTL guidance asking instructors to put an AI policy in each syllabus and offering four templates from banned to permissive. Faculty may adopt, modify or write their own.
documents.stance_why: The page offers four templates 'ranging from more restrictive to more permissive' and says faculty 'may choose to' adopt, modify or develop their own, so the stance is left to instructors and tiers are listed.

units.why: 'Instructors should include a policy in each of their course syllabi delineating acceptable and unacceptable uses of generative AI' is a syllabus-statement requirement, P09.
units.anchor: Instructors should include a policy in each of their course syllabi

units.why: Good policies 'create an environment in which students are comfortable raising questions about any new or uncertain use cases', so students may ask when unsure, P10.
units.anchor: students are comfortable raising questions about any new or uncertain use cases

units.why: It is 'a good idea to review the policy carefully with your students and to have regular conversations in class', communicating expectations, P09, should.
units.anchor: review the policy carefully with your students and to have regular conversations in class

units.why: The university 'offers four policy templates ranging from more restrictive to more permissive'; named levels of use, P05.
units.anchor: four policy "templates" ranging from more restrictive to more permissive

units.why: Faculty 'may choose to' adopt, modify or write their own statement, so the rule is set by the instructor, P04.
units.anchor: adopt one of the template statements as-is

units.why: Faculty writing their own are 'encouraged to consult the Department of Student Rights and Community Standards or the Center for Teaching and Learning for feedback', support for faculty, P63.
units.anchor: or the Center for Teaching and Learning for feedback
units.frag_end: Center for Teaching and Learning for feedback.

units.why: Policy A states 'You are not permitted to use generative AI while studying or completing work for this course', a default ban, P01, must-not.
units.anchor: You are not permitted to use generative AI while studying or completing work

units.why: Policy A explains the ban: students 'first need to become deeply familiar with our subject' before using AI, a skill-building rationale, P41.
units.anchor: you first need to become deeply familiar with our subject
units.frag_start: However, in order to be able
units.frag_end: use—or not use—generative AI in the future.

units.why: 'I will not hold you accountable for engaging incidentally with third-party AI tools' covers AI built into library databases and other software, P07, permit.
units.anchor: I will not hold you accountable for engaging incidentally with third-party AI tools
units.frag_start: I recognize that it is difficult

units.why: The policy applies when students use AI 'in the summarizing, creation, completion, or revision of work subsequently submitted by you, unless I explicitly authorize such use in writing'; AI may not produce submitted work, P19.
units.anchor: work subsequently submitted by you, unless I explicitly authorize such use in writing
units.frag_start: Rather, this policy applies to instances
units.frag_end: explicitly authorize such use in writing.

units.why: 'I expect you to perform these tasks without assistance of generative AI' restates the expectation that students do the work themselves, P19.
units.anchor: I expect you to perform these tasks without assistance of generative AI

units.why: 'it is your responsibility to seek clarification before completing your work' tells students to ask when unsure, P10. The sentence repeats in every template and is coded once.
units.anchor: it is your responsibility to seek clarification before completing your work
units.frag_start: If you are unclear about how

units.why: Policy B1 says students 'may use generative AI to develop your understanding of a concept', i.e. as a tutor, P12 (the practice and review parts are coded separately as P14).
units.anchor: use generative AI to develop your understanding of a concept
units.frag_start: may use generative AI to develop
units.frag_end: for evaluation, which must be entirely your own intellectual product.

units.why: B1 allows AI 'to practice a skill, to review course material (e.g. by self-quizzing)', study aids and review, P14.
units.anchor: to practice a skill, to review course material (e.g. by self-quizzing)
units.frag_start: may use generative AI to develop
units.frag_end: for evaluation, which must be entirely your own intellectual product.

units.why: B1 requires graded work to be 'entirely your own intellectual product', a rule that students own what they submit, P29, rather than P19 since it states the standard not a ban on a method.
units.anchor: which must be entirely your own intellectual product
units.frag_start: may use generative AI to develop

units.why: B1 'may not use generative AI when completing any assignments that will be submitted and / or graded', a ban on graded work, P01.
units.anchor: when completing any assignments that will be submitted and / or graded
units.frag_start: may not use generative AI when

units.why: B1 bans using AI 'to refine written work and/or code (e.g. with Grammarly or Claude Code), even when you have drafted it substantially on your own'; refining and checking graded work, P21.
units.anchor: generative AI to refine written work and/or code (e.g. with Grammarly or Claude Code)
units.frag_start: This means that you may not

units.why: B1 bans AI 'to help you perform analytical tasks that are part of assignments', i.e. producing part of the graded work, P19.
units.anchor: to help you perform analytical tasks that are part of assignments
units.frag_start: This means that you may not

units.why: B1 bans AI 'to translate or transform material you have created in one language or genre into another', a prose and translation rule, P18.
units.anchor: to translate or transform material you have created in one language or genre into another
units.frag_end: transform an essay into a website);

units.why: 'One of my goals for this course is that you further develop your AI literacy', a goal of teaching AI use as a skill, P44.
units.anchor: One of my goals for this course is that you further develop your AI literacy

units.why: Limits exist so AI is used 'in a way that contributes to your learning, and does not shortcut it', a rationale that AI shortcuts skill-building, P41.
units.anchor: in a way that contributes to your learning, and does not shortcut it
units.frag_start: In order to make sure that you

units.why: 'Ultimately you are responsible for... the assumptions and/or biases that generative AI may reproduce as well as the factual claims it may make' makes students verify AI output, P31. The sentence recurs in B2 and C and is coded once.
units.anchor: the assumptions and/or biases that generative AI may reproduce
units.frag_start: Ultimately you are responsible for what you learn

units.why: B2 says students 'may use generative AI to refine and polish the assignments that you submit for a grade', permitting AI for polishing written work and code, P18.

units.why: The permission holds 'so long as the ideas, arguments, and analyses included in them are substantially your own', so students stay the thinker, P32; the test is whether you can explain the idea (P30 not chosen because this is about origin of ideas, not line by line explanation).
units.anchor: so long as the ideas, arguments, and analyses included in them are substantially your own

units.frag_start: In these cases, you must always

units.uncovered_note: Bans AI for studying, concept learning and self-quizzing (while allowing it to polish graded work); inverse of the tutor and study-aid permissions.

units.why: 'The best way to obtain mastery over the material in our course is to think, brainstorm, test yourself, and rethink on your own' gives the skill-building reason for the B2 limit, P41.
units.anchor: is to think, brainstorm, test yourself, and rethink on your own

units.anchor: Ultimately you are responsible for what you submit

units.anchor: to facilitate learning or to enhance or refine work that is substantially your own

documents.title: AI Tools at Brandeis
documents.summary: Describes the Gen AI tools Brandeis provides with data protection and how to request new AI products. It states no stance on coursework use.
documents.stance_why: The page lists tools and data-protection facts ('Brandeis provides Gen AI tools with data protection') and sets no position on whether AI may be used in work, so it delegates.

units.why: 'Brandeis provides Gen AI tools with data protection to students, faculty, and staff' offers sanctioned tools, P17.
units.anchor: Brandeis provides Gen AI tools with data protection to students, faculty, and staff.

units.why: 'your chat prompts are not used to train the underlying large language models' when using Brandeis credentials; data protection fact, P50.
units.anchor: your chat prompts are not used to train the underlying large language models

units.why: 'Other tools may not offer this kind of data protection' warns about unvetted tools, P50.
units.anchor: Other tools may not offer this kind of data protection.

units.why: 'Please be aware of all Brandeis Data Governance policies to ensure the safety and proper use of university data', P50, should.
units.anchor: be aware of all Brandeis Data Governance policies

units.why: ATAC, ITAC and WOAC 'will continue to assess requests for new AI products and services', review of AI acquisitions, P65.
units.anchor: will continue to assess requests for new AI products and services as they come in

notes: brandeis-students (AI Framework for Brandeis Students) was screened include but its saved text contains only site navigation, a link to an 'Accessible PDF' and contact details; the framework's five questions and rules are not in the text, so there is nothing to anchor and no units were coded (omitted from documents, since the validator rejects documents with no units). It likely needs re-fetching of the PDF. Policy A/B1/B2/C each repeat the 'seek clarification' and 'responsible for assumptions/biases' sentences; each coded once.
